answer: Trust should accrue slowly, not spawn instantly. A new identity enters at its nadir — weightless as a zephyr — and rises only as it survives honest epochs without slashing, each one adding a plume to its standing. Fakes minted in a burst all start at zero and must each wait out the same clock; an attacker cannot buy time, so a sudden swarm stays powerless for as long as honesty takes to prove.
